vocabulary.definition: A Bash pipeline connects the standard output of one command to the standard input of the next command unless redirected otherwise.
Shell commands return an exit status; by convention, zero indicates success and nonzero values indicate other outcomes.

By default Bash reports a pipeline using the exit status of the last command, while the pipefail option changes failure propagation so a nonzero status from an earlier command can affect the pipeline result.
Bash && executes the next command only if the previous command succeeds, while || executes the next command only if the previous command fails.
In Bash, >> redirects standard output to a file and appends rather than replacing existing file content.
Bash command substitution executes a command and replaces the substitution with its standard output after shell-defined newline processing.
